Implementation of rules: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - Declares ESLint rule `require-story-annotation` with meta.type="problem", docs.description, fixable="code", hasSuggestions, and JSON schema options including `scope` and `exportPriority`. - Uses shared helpers from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts (DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode) ensuring consistent scope/export semantics. - `create` reads options `{ scope, exportPriority, annotationTemplate, methodAnnotationTemplate, autoFix }` and wires them into `buildVisitors`, so runtime behavior matches documented configuration. - Error message `missingStory` is clear and actionable: "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @story that points to the implementing story file (for example, docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md)." (meets User Experience and Error Location requirements).
- src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - Declares ESLint rule `require-req-annotation` with meta.type="problem", fixable="code", docs.description, messages.missingReq, and schema including `scope` and `exportPriority` mirroring `require-story-annotation`. - Imports and uses the same DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, and shouldProcessNode from helpers/require-story-helpers, ensuring identical function-kind detection and exportPriority behavior. - `create` normalizes options (scope defaulting to DEFAULT_SCOPE, exportPriority defaulting to "all") and defines visitors for: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (excluding MethodDefinition wrappers), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. These are exactly the five node types in REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION. - Each visitor calls `runCheck`, which gates on shouldProcessNode and then delegates to `checkReqAnnotation`, centralizing JSDoc parsing and error reporting. - Error message `missingReq` is explicit and instructive: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE') referencing the appropriate requirement from the story file." (meets User Experience and Error Location requirements).
- Shared helpers for function detection, error location, and scope/export semantics: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - Exports DEFAULT_SCOPE as: ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"] which matches REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION’s required constructs. - Arrow functions are intentionally not included in DEFAULT_SCOPE, so they are excluded from enforcement by default, satisfying "Arrow functions are excluded by default". - Exports STORY_PATH = "docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md" used consistently for annotation templates. - Exports EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - Re-exports DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES and implements: - isExportedNode(node): walks parent chain to detect ExportNamedDeclaration/ExportDefaultDeclaration. - shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority): central gate used by both rules to apply scope + exportPriority logic. Ensures both rules operate on the same function-like constructs and export semantics (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY). - jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory combined via hasStoryAnnotation() to parse/inspect JSDoc and surrounding comments for @story (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING for story annotations). - getReportedFunctionName(node) and getNameNodeForReport(node) used by coreReportMissing/coreReportMethod to (a) derive the human-readable function name and (b) choose the identifier node for error location (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION). - hasStoryAnnotation is wrapped in a try/catch and logs only on error, ensuring malformed JSDoc or unexpected sourceCode behavior does not crash linting (Error Handling criterion). - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts - Provides shared parsing for @req annotations: - getJsdocComment(sourceCode, node), getLeadingComments(node), getCommentsBefore(sourceCode, node), combineComments(leading, before) — common JSDoc/comment accessors (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING for @req). - getFixTargetNode(node) identifies the best AST target (MethodDefinition, VariableDeclarator, ExpressionStatement, or the node itself) for inserting an autofix JSDoc, while preserving structure (Error Handling + Quality Standards for autofix behavior). - createMissingReqFix(node) returns a fixer that inserts "/** @req */\n" before the target (autofix for @req, although current rule disables enableFix by passing { enableFix: false }). - getReportedName and getNameNodeForReqReport derive the function name and location node for error reporting, mirroring the approach used by the @story rule (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION). - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options) composes all of the above: reads sourceCode, collects JSDoc + comments, calls hasReqAnnotation, and if missing, calls reportMissing(context, node, enableFix) (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT via dedicated comment about TS support, REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED for @req).
- Visitor construction for `require-story-annotation`: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts - buildFunctionDeclarationVisitor, buildFunctionExpressionVisitor, buildMethodDefinitionVisitor, buildTSDeclareFunctionVisitor, buildTSMethodSignatureVisitor each: - Check options.shouldProcessNode(node) (shared with require-req-annotation). If true, they call helperReportMissing/helperReportMethod with appropriate annotationTemplate and autoFix toggle. - This ensures enforcement on exactly the desired node types and consistent export-based scoping (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY). - buildArrowFunctionVisitor exists but is gated by shouldProcessNode; since DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include "ArrowFunctionExpression", unannotated arrow functions are excluded by default, matching the story requirement. Tests explicitly assert that unannotated arrow functions are allowed by default. - buildVisitors(...) merges all of these into a single RuleListener used by require-story-annotation.create, satisfying the Core Functionality requirement.

traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md is fully implemented.
Both `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` exist as ESLint rules with: - A shared set of function-like constructs defined by DEFAULT_SCOPE (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), matching REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, and arrow functions excluded by default via the absence of ArrowFunctionExpression from DEFAULT_SCOPE. - Shared, configurable scope and exportPriority semantics using the same helper (shouldProcessNode) and schema definitions, satisfying REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY. - JSDoc/comment parsing for annotations using ESLint’s SourceCode methods and helper functions, fulfilling REQ-JSDOC-PARSING. - Enforcement that in-scope functions must have @story (or accepted @supports/implements) and @req annotations when respective rules are enabled, so enabling both rules forces functions to carry both annotations (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED). - Error messages that are precise, include function names, and provide clear remediation guidance, and error locations anchored at the function identifier or closest equivalent (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, User Experience criterion). - Dedicated support and tests for TypeScript constructs (TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) via visitors and shared annotation-checker utilities (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT, Integration criterion).
Extensive unit tests, helper edge-case tests, and rule documentation for both rules confirm they meet all acceptance criteria (Core Functionality, Quality Standards, Integration, User Experience, Error Handling, Documentation). The passing Jest test suite provides strong evidence that the functionality behaves as required in both JavaScript and TypeScript codebases.
